nary_nodes.label: Castel's mission to be world champion daily
evidence: "I have a mission: to be the world champion every day in my shop for my customers," he said, eyes twinkling.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel to open new venue in Paris
evidence: Alongside his daughter Margot, he is set to open a new venue in Paris in September – a cross between a café, a restaurant and a bakery-patisserie.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel collaborates with artists for Yule logs
evidence: Always in search of new inspiration, Castel also collaborates with artists to create Yule logs. "Because they're not technically limited in their ideas, it pushes us to try new things," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel discovers breadmaking in 2012
evidence: When Castel set out on his own in 2012 after working with chef Hélène Darroze, at the prestigious Hotel Costes and La Grande Epicerie de Paris, he discovered the art of breadmaking.

Three years after fellow French pastry chef Nina Métayer was crowned champion, Castel received the UIBC award presented annually to a leading figure in the profession in recognition of their career and contribution to the trade on July 14 in Singapore.
The smell of warm bread hangs in the air at one of Benoît Castel's patisseries in Paris, where the newly crowned world's best pastry chef was hard at work testing new recipes.
"Our work is no trivial matter, every day we make things that people put into their bodies," said Castel, who hails from Brittany in western France.
As a novice, he created his famous 'pain du coin', made from a variety of flours, natural quince sourdough starter, honey and Salish salt from the US Pacific Northwest.
This was followed by 'the bread of yesterday and tomorrow', made from the previous day's unsold stock as part of an anti-waste initiative.
